subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acmehealth.com>, Michael Soto <michael.soto@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps

Hi Emily / Michael —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Pain / goals you shared:
- Latency spikes during peak appointment-booking windows (50–200 rps); target p95 latency < 200ms for user-facing flows.
- Data isolation / HIPAA concerns: all inference must be isolated from multi-tenant hosts and keys managed by customer KMS/HSM.
- Predictable unit economics: need a committed-reserved option to avoid unpredictable overage costs.
- Region & residency: primary region must be US East, with DR in US West.

Proposed Dedicated capacity profile (initial):
- Reserved pool: 4x A100-class GPUs (reserved capacity) in US-East (option to increase to 8x for Q4).
- Baseline throughput: ~50 rps (concurrent conversational workloads), burst capacity up to ~200 rps via configured burst/eviction policy and spare capacity pools.
- Isolation: customer-dedicated tenant + optional single-tenant physical host placement.
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime; p95 latency objective <200ms for our optimized model runtime under typical prompting patterns.
- Compliance: Redwood supports SOC 2, HIPAA patterns, and customer-managed KMS (we’ll surface encryption & key rotation details in the security call).

Next steps / asks:
1) I’ve attached a draft MAP (mutual action plan) and our initial pricing PDF for Dedicated. Please review and flag any changes.
2) Security deep-dive: can your security/infrastructure team join a 45–60m call next week?
3) Confirm expected peak windows (days/times) and any batch/background inference that should be isolated.

I’ll follow up with a few proposed times for the security call.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf, MAP_acme_health_draft.docx

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- HIPAA compliance is critical for us; we’ll need written confirmation around data handling, BAAs, and support for customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Residency: US East primary with failover to US West is correct.
- Autoscaling: curious how burst capacity works in practice and how we’re charged for short spikes versus sustained usage.
- Peak windows: weekdays 08:00–11:00 ET and 17:00–20:00 ET; weekend volume is low but we do occasional batch jobs overnight.

Can we schedule the security deep-dive on Wed May 19? CC’ing our infra lead Michael and infra@acmehealth so they can propose times.

> Thanks Ben — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
> 
> - HIPAA compliance is critical for us; we’ll need written confirmation around data handling, BAAs, and support for customer-managed KMS/HSM.
> - Residency: US East primary with failover to US West is correct.
> - Autoscaling: curious how burst capacity works in practice and how we’re charged for short spikes versus sustained usage.
> - Peak windows: weekdays 08:00–11:00 ET and 17:00–20:00 ET; weekend volume is low but we do occasional batch jobs overnight.

Thanks — quick answers below and I’ve attached a short security questionnaire draft to speed the deep-dive: security_qs_acme.xlsx

- HIPAA & BAAs: Redwood has a HIPAA addendum we can attach to the SOW; we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations (we’ll provide architecture diagrams during the security call).
- Isolation: Dedicated pools are tenant-isolated. For stronger guarantees we can offer single-tenant physical host placements for an additional fee — we’ll note options in the MAP.
- Autoscale & burst pricing: reserved capacity covers a baseline (committed monthly GPU-hours). Bursts are charged as metered overage at discounted burst rates; short spikes under the configured burst window (e.g., <5m) can be absorbed by our warm spare pool without immediate metering depending on policy (we’ll detail options).
- Peak scheduling: thanks for the windows — we’ll include those in the MAP and sizing assumptions.

Proposed security deep-dive: Wed May 19, 10:00 AM ET (45m). Does that work for your infra team?

Next steps I’ll take care of:
- Update MAP with peak windows, baseline/burst numbers and single-tenant option.
- Share SOW template + HIPAA addendum for legal review.

Ben
